Timers and the rendering-related scheduling of HTML: setTimeout / setInterval (with the HTML nesting clamp and background throttling), requestAnimationFrame, requestIdleCallback, and the page's visibility. Timestamps given to callbacks are on the performance.now() timeline of the page.

Exposed to: Window, Worker. Source: api/timers.widl.

Odin: import "wren:timers".

#Types

#handle Timer

A pending timeout or interval.

Checked by the browser on every call (lookup_Timer).

#callback TimerHandler

void TimerHandler(i32 user)

#callback TimerHandler64

void TimerHandler64(i64 user)

A timer callback with a 64-bit user value.

#callback FrameRequestCallback

void FrameRequestCallback(i32 user, f64 time)

An animation frame callback: time is the frame's time on the page's performance timeline.

#callback IdleRequestCallback

void IdleRequestCallback(i32 user, f64 deadline, bool did_timeout)

An idle callback: run before deadline (performance timeline), or late because its timeout expired.

#enum VisibilityState : i32

Whether the page is shown.

membervalue
Visible0
Hidden1
